Alyssa: :wave: hey team — first week, quick question about org lanes. Who "owns" the model-serving routing policies (the rules that decide hosted vs dedicated routing + fallbacks)? Also who do I call if a new model rollout starts returning 500s and we need to rollback ASAP? My manager said ask here so I know who to ping.
Jordan: Hey Alyssa — welcome! short answer: routing policy config lives with eng-runtime, but Dedicated routing decisions (capacity/tenant routing) are governed by the Dedicated product team. For rollbacks, infra oncall usually triggers the emergency rollback, but eng-runtime owns the rollback playbook.
Priya: +1 to Jordan. In practice:
- config changes: eng-runtime (cc @Infra SRE for infra-level changes)
- canary/rollouts: product-release + eng-runtime
- incident rollback: infra-sre will execute and coordinate with eng-runtime and the owning model team
Alyssa: ok thanks — who on eng-runtime should I add to my contact list? any docs I should read first?
Jordan: ping @Luis (he's the runtime PM) and @Priya for rollout questions. Luis is around for quick context.
Luis: hi Alyssa — welcome again. The short doc is here: https://redwood.company/docs/serving-routing-matrix and the escalation matrix is below. Read the sections "Rollouts" and "Emergency Rollback" first.
Luis: ```
Escalation (quick):
1) Pager -> infra-sre (primary)
2) If infra-sre can't remediate -> eng-oncall (runtime)
3) Product + owning-model-team notified for postmortem and customer comms
Contact order (if pager fails): Luis -> Priya -> Jordan
```
Alyssa: great, that helps. For the doc link I don't have access yet — what permission group do I need?
Priya: you should already have access via the "redwood-employees" group, but if not, open a ticket to it-requests with subject "doc access: serving-routing-matrix" and tag me. I'll approve.
Alyssa: perfect, filing the ticket now. One more: who signs off on production changes that affect latency SLOs? Is that infra or product?
Jordan: sign-off depends on change type. If it's infra-level (kernel, scheduler, routing infra) infra-sre + eng-platform. If it's model/serving config that changes token cost or latency behavior, eng-runtime + product. For high-risk changes we require a release owner and a canary window.
Alyssa: got it — thanks everyone! tagging notes to my onboarding doc. :thumbsup:
oncall-bot: Reminder: Alyssa your new-hire intro with Runtime team is scheduled Thu 10:00am. Join: https://meet.redwood/intro-runtime
Infra SRE: adding myself in case you need pager handoff guidance — infra-sre primary is paged for sev2+/rollback. DM me if you want the cheat-sheet."
